gloss: to open up; to warm up to

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {打|う}ち{解|と}けませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {打|う}ち{解|と}けていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {打|う}ち{解|と}けていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to open up; to warm up to; to become friendly
definitions.explanation: to relax one's guard and become comfortable or friendly with someone

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はすぐに{打|う}ち{解|と}けた。
examples.english: He quickly warmed up to everyone.

examples.japanese: {最初|さいしょ}は{緊張|きんちょう}していたが、{話|はな}すうちに{打|う}ち{解|と}けた。
examples.english: I was nervous at first, but I opened up as we talked.

examples.japanese: {打|う}ち{解|と}けた{雰囲気|ふんいき}の{中|なか}で{会議|かいぎ}が{進|すす}んだ。
examples.english: The meeting proceeded in a relaxed atmosphere.

notes:
{打|う}ち{解|と}ける is a compound verb combining {打|う}つ (to strike) + {解|と}ける (to loosen), expressing the breaking down of barriers between people.

VERB TYPE:
- Ichidan verb (る-verb)
- Intransitive

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {打|う}ち{解|と}けた{雰囲気|ふんいき} (relaxed atmosphere)
- {打|う}ち{解|と}けた{関係|かんけい} (friendly relationship)
- すぐに{打|う}ち{解|と}ける (to quickly warm up)
- なかなか{打|う}ち{解|と}けない (to not easily open up)
- ～と{打|う}ち{解|と}ける (to warm up to ~)

USAGE NOTES:
- Often describes the process of becoming comfortable with new people
- The adjective form {打|う}ち{解|と}けた is commonly used to describe atmospheres and relationships
- Implies overcoming initial awkwardness or formality

RELATED TERMS:
- {親|した}しくなる (to become close)
- {仲良|なかよ}くなる (to become friendly)
- {心|こころ}を{開|ひら}く (to open one's heart)
- {氷|こおり}が{解|と}ける (the ice breaks - idiom)

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in everyday conversation.
